title: XML Entity Expansion, External Entities, and Regex Backtracking
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library; xml.etree is vulnerable to expansion but raises on external entity retrieval, unlike xml.sax and xml.dom
security_mechanism: Entity declarations in a DTD let a small document reference itself recursively: xml.etree and xml.sax still perform recursive entity expansion (billion-laughs) and quadratic blowup, so a few hundred bytes expand to gigabytes in memory. xml.sax and xml.dom additionally resolve external entities to file:// or http:// targets, giving local file read and SSRF. The same shape of unbounded work exists in re: a crafted input against a vulnerable pattern drives exponential backtracking on one CPU core with no timeout mechanism.

source_sink_clues.source: XML documents uploaded or posted by clients; regex patterns and subject strings supplied by users.
source_sink_clues.sink: xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring/parse, xml.sax.parse/parseString, xml.dom.minidom.parseString on untrusted documents; re.match/search with attacker-influenced pattern or unbounded subject

tracking_guards: Verify parsing goes through defusedxml (or an explicit parser with DTD and entity processing disabled) rather than the stdlib defaults; for regex, verify the pattern is a compile-time constant, subject length is capped, and the pattern has no nested quantifiers over overlapping alternations.
not_candidate_when: XML comes from a trusted internal producer and DTDs are absent by construction, or defusedxml is used; the regex pattern is constant with no nested quantifiers and the input length is bounded to a few kilobytes.
synthetic_safe_example: import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET; tree = ET.fromstring(xml_payload)
public_references: CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/776.html
CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html
